headline: NASA awards Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis
summary: NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis.
A US intelligence report has described Iran as an emerging space power.
Telesat in Canada has pushed full Lightspeed service to mid-2028, and KT SAT will lead a South Korean maritime connectivity project.
ESA's outpost studies stand ahead of a committee vote on the tenth of November and the Council in Rome on the fifteenth of December.
Blue Origin's New Glenn return is reported for January 2027 and is not confirmed by the company.
bottom_line: The ESA path towards Rome stands at studies awarded and no new Council decision. The next date that matters is the tenth of November committee vote.

global.title: NASA awards Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis
global.summary: NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to three commercial operators. Values and terms are not in the material held.
global.why: Commercial operators now sit inside NASA's relay supply. The terms are what will show how large the shift is.
global.bar: Headline only; no values. Look for NASA page.

global.title: Telesat delays Lightspeed full service entry to mid-2028
global.summary: Telesat has moved full Lightspeed service to mid-2028. Its chief executive addressed the launch crunch and sovereign demand.
global.why: A later start narrows the window for sovereign broadband customers. Launch availability is the stated pressure.
global.bar: Company statement via trade press; a week old.

global.title: FCC names Courtney Reinhard Space Bureau chief and moves on direct-to-device rules
global.summary: The FCC has named a new Space Bureau chief. It also looks to update direct-to-device rules and auction more spectrum.
global.why: Licensing and spectrum rules shape US satellite operators. The bureau chief will run that work.

items.title: ESA investigates a European-led orbital outpost
items.summary: ESA announced studies of a possible European-led orbital outpost on the third of November. No new Council decision has followed. A committee vote is due on the tenth of November, then Rome on the fifteenth of December.
items.why: The studies feed the Rome meeting. Money and a plan are still not adopted.
items.bar: Vote date from thread, not packet.

items.title: Ukraine's satellite communications stay tied to Starshield
items.summary: A mid-2027 Starshield contract hope has been stated, with no government statement on the October close approaches. Lithuanian press frames Ukraine's satellite position as a race against time. No date is set.
items.why: Ukraine's dependence on one provider is the live question. No official date exists to test it.
items.bar: Standing item; Breaking Defense not in packet.

items.title: Norway's space directorate and Canada's space agency sign an Arctic agreement
items.summary: The agreement allows closer space cooperation in the Arctic. Sweden holds its national space day on the eighteenth of February, 2027.
items.why: Arctic coverage is the shared interest. The Swedish date is the next fixed one in the region.

items.title: ITU accepts Open Cosmos extension but halves its broadband constellation
items.summary: The International Telecommunication Union accepted the extension and cut the planned constellation size by half.
items.why: A smaller filing limits the operator's planned capacity. It is a rare regulator cut.

items.title: ArianeGroup reports second SyLEx launch; Ariane 6 Amazon Leo flight set for 23 November at earliest
items.summary: ArianeGroup reported a second successful SyLEx sounding rocket launch on the fourth of November. Arianespace plans 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the tenth Ariane 6 flight from the twenty-third of November at the earliest.
items.why: The Ariane 6 date is the next European launch marker. SyLEx supports the French M51 missile line.

items.title: Armenia honours Axiom Space co-founder Kam Ghaffarian
items.summary: Ghaffarian has been awarded the State Prize in IT and is visiting Armenia. No dated space event is on file for the region.
items.why: It is a link between Armenia and a commercial station builder. Nothing dated follows.

items.title: US intelligence report describes Iran as an emerging space power
items.summary: A US intelligence report describes Iran as an emerging space power. The report's contents beyond that description are not in the material held.
items.why: It frames Iran's program as a US security concern. The detail will matter more than the label.

items.title: Türkiye sets 2027 and 2028 satellite launches; budget proposal stands
items.summary: A joint satellite of Turkic states is due in 2027 and a new micro-satellite in 2028. The 2027 space and aviation budget proposal is TL 24.59 billion, with no split published.
items.why: Two launch years are now on the calendar. The budget split decides what funds them.

items.title: Australian Broadcasting Corporation says NASA's Swift fell over Indonesia
items.summary: The broadcaster says Swift fell over Indonesia on the fifth of November. Spanish trade press places the break-up over Sumatra. No NASA page confirms it.
items.why: Swift's mission is over on press accounts. The NASA statement is still missing.

items.title: KT SAT to lead South Korean maritime connectivity project with ST Engineering iDirect
items.summary: KT SAT will lead a maritime connectivity project in South Korea with ST Engineering iDirect.
items.why: It adds a Korean operator to maritime service. Terms are not in the material held.

items.title: Financial Times says Blue Origin's New Glenn returns in January 2027
items.summary: The Financial Times, carried by Reuters and Bloomberg, says New Glenn returns in January 2027. Blue Origin has not confirmed. The FAA comment deadline of the thirtieth of October passed with no decision on file.
items.why: A slip would push back Blue Origin's cadence plans. Only the company or the FAA can settle it.
items.bar: CHECK: packet holds no FT/Reuters URL; link is placeholder. Fix or drop before publication.

items.title: US midterm result returns Democrats to Congress; trade press weighs NASA and Golden Dome
items.summary: Infoespacial asks what the Democratic return to Congress means for NASA and Golden Dome. A former defence official warned Golden Dome may not outlive the Trump presidency.
items.why: Budget control shapes both programs. No vote date is on file.
items.bar: Opinion and analysis, not a decision.

audio_script: Good morning. It is Friday, the sixth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis. A US intelligence report has described Iran as an emerging space power. And NASA's Swift observatory has come down over Indonesia. NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis. The award was announced on the fourth of November. All three are commercial satellite operators, so commercial relay capacity now sits inside NASA's communications supply. Contract values and terms have not been published in the material we hold. The next NASA date is the eighth of December, when commercial space-station proposals are due. In Europe, ESA announced on the third of November studies of a possible European-led orbital outpost in low Earth orbit. No new Council decision has followed. A committee vote is due on the tenth of November, and the Council meets in Rome on the fifteenth of December. In Central and Eastern Europe, Ukraine's satellite communications remain tied to Starshield. A mid-2027 contract hope has been stated. There is no government statement on the October close approaches, and no date is set. In Norway, the space directorate and the Canadian Space Agency have signed a new agreement on closer cooperation in the Arctic. Norway also signed the declaration on the European Union's ISOS in-orbit servicing program on the tenth of June. In Sweden, the national space day will be held on the eighteenth of February, 2027. In Spain, the International Telecommunication Union has accepted an extension for Open Cosmos, but has halved the size of its planned broadband constellation. In France, ArianeGroup reported a second successful SyLEx sounding rocket launch on the fourth of November. Arianespace plans to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the tenth Ariane 6 flight on the twenty-third of November at the earliest. In Armenia, Axiom Space co-founder Kam Ghaffarian has been awarded the State Prize in IT and is visiting the country. No dated space event is on file for the region. In Iran, a US intelligence report, covered on the fifth of November, describes the country as an emerging space power. In Türkiye, a joint satellite of the Turkic states is due in 2027, and a new micro-satellite in 2028. The 2027 space and aviation budget proposal stands at TL 24.59 billion, with no split published. In Indonesia, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation says Swift fell over the country on the fifth of November. Spanish trade press places the break-up over Sumatra. No NASA page confirms it. In South Korea, KT SAT will lead a maritime connectivity project with ST Engineering iDirect. In Japan, the Martian Moons eXploration probe remains on its transfer orbit towards Mars, with no arrival date on file. In the United States, the midterm result returns Democrats to Congress, and trade press is weighing what that means for NASA and Golden Dome. The Financial Times says Blue Origin's New Glenn returns in January 2027. Blue Origin has not confirmed it. The Federal Aviation Administration comment deadline of the thirtieth of October has passed with no decision on file. In Mexico, commentary continues on the national space program for 2026 to 2030, with no new date on file. What we are tracking this week: the ESA committee vote on the tenth of November, any NASA page on Swift, and any Blue Origin confirmation of its return date. What we are tracking this month: the Ariane 6 flight with Amazon Leo satellites, on the twenty-third of November at the earliest. The heads-up dates are the eighth of December for NASA station proposals, the fifteenth of December for the Council in Rome, and January 2027 for the reported New Glenn return. Two further items are worth holding in mind. In Canada, Telesat has moved full Lightspeed service to mid-2028, citing the launch crunch and sovereign demand. In the United States, the Federal Communications Commission has named a new Space Bureau chief and is looking to update direct-to-device rules and auction more spectrum. That is the briefing for Friday, the sixth of November.
